newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said most traders were sidelined ahead of the outcome of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Senate Humphrey-Hawkins testimony tonight.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. The market is now waiting for fresh clues to market direction from Alan Greenspan's Senate speech later tonight," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact as he is not expected to say anything that is going to move the market," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday, Thursday/Friday and week-fixed were unchanged from Tuesday's common 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent and three-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent. Nine-months rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent and twelve-months rose 1/16 point to 6 5-7/8 percent. - P. Theseira (65-870-3085)
